lesson_title: Roller Coaster Physics: Only the Drop Counts
hook_text: Steep ramp vs lazy slope, same height. Who's faster at the bottom? Everyone gets this wrong.
clip_script: Two ramps drop into the same bowl. One is a steep, scary, almost-vertical face. The other is a long, lazy slope. Both start 5 metres above the bottom. Two skaters roll from rest, one down each ramp. Who is moving faster at the bottom? Neither. Both arrive at exactly 9,90 metres per second. The steep-ramp skater gets there sooner — steeper means the trade happens fast — but not faster. Speed at the bottom is bought entirely with height, and both skaters spent the same 5 metres. The path is just the shape of the shop; the price and the purchase are the same.
visual_style: Split screen: two skaters on ramps of wildly different shapes dropping the same height; speedometers at the bottom lock onto the identical 9,90 as the clocks show different times.
pacing: Quick setup of the race, a beat of suspense on the question, double-speedometer reveal.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and run the 200 kg roller coaster from crest to bottom yourself.
